title: Lori Trahan — Campaign loans and disclosures
outcome: No excessive contribution found. No further action on disclosure errors.
summary: The Committee received an OCE referral on September 18, 2019, extended review on November 4, and published the referral on December 17. It found that Trahan funded the loans with personal funds under her prenuptial agreement and found no evidence that disclosure errors or omissions were knowing and willful. It voted on July 15, 2020 to dismiss and closed the matter upon publication. In related matters, the FEC found no reason to believe Trahan knowingly accepted excessive contributions and used prosecutorial discretion to dismiss separate reporting and deposit allegations against her campaign committee and treasurer.

title: Rashida Tlaib — 2018 campaign salary
outcome: Committee directed $10,800 repayment. FEC confirmed reimbursement and dismissed.
summary: Following a 2019 OCE referral and further review, the Committee concluded that $10,800 of post-election compensation covered periods when Tlaib was no longer a candidate and directed her to reimburse her campaign. The Committee voted on July 23, 2020 to take no further action subject to completion. The FEC later confirmed reimbursement from campaign disclosures and dismissed under its prosecutorial discretion.

title: Roger Williams — FAST Act amendment
outcome: No House rule or law violated. Committee dismissed.
summary: OCE referred the matter on May 13, 2016. The Committee reviewed whether Williams sponsored an amendment that affected auto dealerships, including his own. It found that sponsorship did not violate a law or House rule, advised that he should have sought guidance, and unanimously dismissed the matter.

title: David Schweikert — House reprimand and fine
outcome: House reprimand and $50,000 fine under adopted report. Related FEC settlements involved other respondents.
summary: The Committee received referrals in 2018 and expanded its subcommittee inquiry. Schweikert admitted 11 violations involving campaign finance and disclosure, official resources, campaign work by staff, and lack of candor. The House adopted the Committee report on July 31, 2020, implementing the reprimand and $50,000 fine. In the related FEC matter, the campaign committee agreed to a $125,000 civil penalty and former staffer Richard Oliver Schwab agreed to $7,500.

title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez — 2021 Met Gala gifts and payments
outcome: Impermissible gifts and delayed payment. Additional payments directed.
summary: The Committee received the OCE referral in June 2022. Its July 2025 report found that Ocasio-Cortez accepted impermissible goods and services connected to the 2021 Met Gala and delayed appropriate payment. It did not find knowing or willful violations. It directed additional payments of $2,733.28 to the designer and $250 to the Costume Institute for her guest’s meal. The report made closure conditional on payment.

title: Jimmy Gomez — House conduct report
outcome: Committee found violations of clauses 1 and 18(b). Any House sanction requires separate House action.
summary: The Committee announced its review on August 17, 2026. On November 19 it adopted a report finding that Gomez made unwelcome sexual advances toward a House staffer in violation of the Code of Official Conduct. Gomez maintained that contact was consensual. The Committee released the report on November 23 and left any sanction to the House.

title: Mike Kelly — Cleveland-Cliffs stock purchase review
category: Confidential information and conflict of interest
outcome: Committee report served as reproval. Divestment was recommended.
summary: After a July 2021 OCE referral, the Committee reviewed a Cleveland-Cliffs stock purchase by Kelly’s spouse. It did not find substantial evidence of an insider-trading or conflict-of-interest violation. It found substantial evidence of a Code of Official Conduct violation and criticized Kelly’s conduct during the investigation, including untimely disclosure of an additional purchase. The report adopted July 22, 2025 served as a reproval and recommended divestment and donation of any profits to charity.

title: Wesley Hunt — Campaign spending review
outcome: Committee closed the inquiry and took no further action.
summary: OCE referred campaign spending allegations on March 25, 2024. The Committee extended review in May, released the referral and Hunt’s response on June 24, and announced closure on December 30. Its public statement covered several members and described compliance problems in some cases without identifying individual findings.

title: Ronny Jackson — Campaign spending review
outcome: Committee closed the inquiry and took no further action.
summary: The Committee received OCE referrals on December 22, 2021 and March 25, 2024 about the same campaign spending allegations. It published referral materials in May 2022 and June 2024. On December 30, 2024, it announced closure. Its public statement covered several members and described compliance problems in some cases without identifying individual findings.

title: Gwen Moore — 2014 protest citation review
outcome: Committee declined to impanel an investigative subcommittee.
summary: Moore received a disorderly conduct citation following a September 4, 2014 protest in West Milwaukee. The Committee considered the matter on September 10 and declined to form an investigative subcommittee. Its report described a prospective fine. Final court disposition and payment were not confirmed.

title: Pat Fallon — Periodic transaction report review
outcome: Committee unanimously dismissed the referral after remedial steps.
summary: OCE referred Fallon’s periodic transaction reports on March 2, 2022. The Committee extended review on April 18 and released referral materials on May 31. The Committee found no clear evidence the errors and omissions were knowing or willful, noted remedial efforts, and dismissed the referral.

title: Victoria Spartz — Airport citation review
outcome: Virginia charge dismissed. Committee took no further action. TSA civil penalty paid, as reported by Committee.
summary: Spartz was cited at Dulles on June 28, 2024 and charged on July 11. The Committee reported that she completed a gun safety course, the charge was dismissed on September 20 by nolle prosequi, and she paid a separate TSA civil penalty. The Committee declined to impanel a subcommittee and closed the matter.

title: Al Green — 2021 protest arrest review
outcome: Committee took no further action.
summary: The Committee considered Green’s August 3, 2021 protest-related arrest and declined to form a subcommittee. The Committee reported that Green intended to pay $50 and that local proceedings were expected to end without further action. The Committee closed its own matter on publication.

title: Gregory W. Meeks — Loan and disclosure review
outcome: Committee closed its investigation. Disclosure noncompliance was inadvertent. The improper-gift allegation was not substantiated.
summary: After a May 2011 OCE referral, the Committee dismissed allegations concerning the separate investment-firm loan. It found that Meeks had inadvertently omitted the $40,000 Ahmad loan from two financial disclosures, which he later amended. It closed the improper-gift inquiry after it could not substantiate that allegation.

title: Ilhan Omar — Financial disclosure and book advance review
outcome: OCE recommended dismissal and transmitted no findings. Committee ended review.
summary: The Committee received the OCE referral on December 22, 2021 about financial disclosure and a possible book advance. OCE unanimously recommended dismissal and transmitted no findings. A majority of the Committee did not vote to dismiss, but the Committee stated that it would not review the matter further.

title: Pramila Jayapal — 2018 protest arrest review
outcome: Committee took no further action. Local charge disposed of after $50 collateral forfeiture.
summary: The Committee considered Jayapal’s June 28, 2018 protest-related arrest. It reported that she forfeited $50 in collateral and that the local court disposed of the charge. The Committee declined to form an investigative subcommittee and closed the matter.

title: Chuck Edwards — House censure
outcome: House censured Edwards on September 1, 2026.
summary: The Committee announced its review in May 2026 and issued a report in August concluding there was substantial reason to believe Edwards violated House rules related to sexual harassment and a hostile workplace. Edwards disagreed with the findings and waived certain procedural steps. The Committee recommended censure and the House imposed it by adopting H. Res. 1498, 413–2.

title: Troy E. Nehls — Campaign finance reproval
outcome: Committee adopted a report serving as a reproval.
summary: OCE referred the matter on December 11, 2023. The Committee extended review in March 2024 and published referral materials in May. It reviewed transactions involving campaign office rent and payments through Nehls’ company, found that use of an unregistered entity led to improper contributions, incomplete reporting and expenditures with an unverifiable campaign purpose, and adopted a reproval on November 19, 2026. Nehls disputed some of the report’s factual and legal conclusions.

title: Judy Chu — Public letter of reproval
outcome: Committee issued a public letter of reproval.
summary: The Committee investigated the use of official resources for campaign work and Chu’s communications with staff during the inquiry. It issued a public letter of reproval for her violations of House rules, including interference with the investigation, and closed the matter upon publication.

title: Joyce Beatty — 2021 protest arrest review
outcome: Committee took no further action. Beatty reported paying $50.
summary: The Committee considered Beatty’s July 15, 2021 protest-related arrest and declined to form a subcommittee. Beatty told the Committee she had paid $50 before release. The Committee closed its review upon publication.

title: Sam Graves — Committee hearing witness review
outcome: Committee found no House rule or standard of conduct violated.
summary: After an August 2009 OCE referral, the Committee reviewed Graves’ approval of a hearing witness who had investments in common with his wife. The Committee found no applicable rule or standard was violated and identified no evidence that the hearing or testimony resulted in action that could benefit Graves, his wife, or the witness.

title: Judy Chu — 2022 protest arrest review
outcome: Committee took no further action.
summary: The Committee considered Chu’s June 30, 2022 protest-related arrest and declined to form a subcommittee. It reported that Chu intended to pay $50 and that local proceedings were expected to end without further action. The Committee closed its own matter upon publication.

title: Maxine Waters — OneUnited Bank review
outcome: Committee took no further action against Waters. Her chief of staff received a separate reproval.
summary: The Committee reviewed Waters’ request for a Treasury meeting after a 2009 OCE referral. Outside counsel reviewed the matter and the Committee concluded the evidence did not support further action against Waters. The Committee issued a letter of reproval to her chief of staff, Mikael Moore, for his conduct.

title: Bill Huizenga — Campaign recordkeeping
outcome: Committee found a House rule violation and took no further action.
summary: After an August 2019 OCE referral, the Committee found that inadequate campaign recordkeeping led to a violation of clause 6 of the Code of Official Conduct. It did not find clear personal use of campaign funds, recognized corrective efforts, and unanimously took no further action.

title: Mike Collins — Intern compensation and staff oversight
outcome: Committee found improper office practices and agreed on a $2,880 return to Treasury.
summary: The Committee received an OCC referral on October 7, 2025 and published it in January 2026. It found improper intern compensation and acceptance of volunteer services and identified potentially improper staff travel reimbursements without finding substantial evidence of misuse for that travel. The report adopted November 19 called for $2,880 to be returned to Treasury and closed the matter.

title: Lauren Boebert — House chamber mask rule fine (February 15, 2022)
outcome: Fine notice published after appeal period expired.
summary: The Committee received notice on February 15, 2022 that the Sergeant at Arms fined Boebert under H. Res. 38, the House chamber mask rule. The Committee reported that Boebert did not appeal by the deadline.

title: Lauren Boebert — House chamber mask rule fine (November 30, 2021)
outcome: Fine notice published after appeal period expired.
summary: The Committee received notice on November 30, 2021 that the Sergeant at Arms fined Boebert under H. Res. 38, the House chamber mask rule. The Committee reported that Boebert did not appeal by the deadline.

outcome: Appeal did not receive majority support.
summary: The Committee received notice on May 20, 2021 that the Sergeant at Arms fined Duyne under H. Res. 38, the House chamber mask rule. Duyne appealed on May 24, 2021. The appeal did not receive majority support, so the fine was upheld under the applicable rule.

title: Ralph Norman — House chamber mask rule fine (May 20, 2021)
outcome: Appeal did not receive majority support.
summary: The Committee received notice on May 20, 2021 that the Sergeant at Arms fined Norman under H. Res. 38, the House chamber mask rule. Norman appealed on June 16, 2021. The appeal did not receive majority support, so the fine was upheld under the applicable rule. The subsequent federal civil challenge was dismissed on Speech or Debate Clause grounds, and the Supreme Court denied review in 2024.

summary: The Committee received notice on August 25, 2021 that the Sergeant at Arms fined Huizenga under H. Res. 73, the House chamber security screening rule. Huizenga appealed on September 24, 2021. A majority of the Committee agreed to the appeal on October 21, 2021.

outcome: Committee agreed to the appeal.
summary: The Committee received notice on September 27, 2021 that the Sergeant at Arms fined Crenshaw under H. Res. 73, the House chamber security screening rule. Crenshaw appealed on September 30, 2021. A majority of the Committee agreed to the appeal on October 21, 2021.

title: Virginia Foxx — House chamber security screening rule fine (May 14, 2021)

summary: The Committee received notice on May 14, 2021 that the Sergeant at Arms fined Foxx under H. Res. 73, the House chamber security screening rule. Foxx appealed on June 1, 2021. A majority of the Committee agreed to the appeal on June 29, 2021.

title: Thomas R. Suozzi — Periodic transaction report review
outcome: Committee unanimously dismissed the referral after remedial steps.
summary: The Committee received an OCE referral on February 28, 2022 concerning timely periodic transaction reports. It extended review in April and released the referral and Suozzi’s response on July 29. The Committee unanimously dismissed the referral after finding no clear evidence the errors or omissions were knowing or willful and noting remedial efforts.
